tone.quote: Deg wayen yerzan tiɣra, d nutenti i d ul n yal tantala, imi ulac tanḍawit seg tantala ɣer tayeḍ gar-asent. a u i ... yiwet d tis 4 ur tettwaḥsab ara d tiɣri di tjeṛṛumt, tella kan akken ad tsishel lmenṭeq mi ara yili mlallent ta ɣer tama n ta, neɣ ugar n snat n tergalin. Degmi i as-qqaren tiɣri tuɣliqt (e).
tone.translation: As for the vowels, they are the core of every dialect, since there is no variation from one dialect to another among them: a, u, i ... a fourth one is not counted as a vowel in the grammar; it is there only to ease pronunciation when consonants come next to one another, or more than two consonants. That is why it is called the closed vowel (e). [segmental statement only; the work has no passage on tone or accent]
